So let's first establish a few basic facts of the situation.

1) Chaos Space Marines do use bolters from time to time.

2) Standard bolter rounds are essentially tiny rockets, using integrated fuel to propel themselves forward.

3) Bolters themselves are pretty complex to produce, but we can reasonably assume that CSM have maintained their existing bolters from before the Horus Heresy and/or captured more over time.

4) Bolter rounds are also relatively complex to produce, however since they are expended when used then rounds would require continuous production(or at least acquisition) somewhere in order for 1) to be true.

5) The forces of Chaos have probably captured at least one forge world capable of making bolter ammunition.

But here's where it all breaks down:

6) It would be prohibitively time consuming and/or inefficient for CSM to scrounge their own unexpended bolter rounds from Imperial worlds as their primary source of ammunition.

7) Even if a captured forge world is making new rounds, the forces of Chaos do not have any organization even remotely resembling the Adeptus Munitorum to distribute those rounds to CSM throughout the galaxy.

So this leaves the question. From where do Chaos Space Marines get their Bolter rounds? Thoughts Voat?

Grocery store manager. I'm not the head manager (most grocery stores have a few store level management positions). I can't complain. Good benefits, decent pay and because I'm management I have a set schedule. People are freaks about their groceries though and take stores not having something very personally. And a lot of high school and college kids work in them so sometimes it's like herding cats for a living.

Edit: I missed the question of how I got in and do I recommend it. Basically after the Navy I was a career restaurant worker. I've worked kitchen, front of the house, bar tender. It was fun for a time but as I was hitting my late 20's I realized I needed something with benefits and more room for advancement. Someone said I should look into grocery stores and the one I worked for had everything I wanted and I knew because i was a bit older and experienced then most of the employees I could move up fast.

Do I recommend it? Like all customer service jobs it has it's drawbacks and a lot of people wash out fast. Be able to deal with assholes with a smile on your face and move really fast! If you can stick it out and work up to even a dept. manager it's great. Unlike other customer service jobs everyone is eligible for benefits from the courtesy clerks (baggers) to management. Entry level work with full benefits is more and more rare these days.

I am a food chemist. I took a lot of chemistry and biology classes in college. I actually originally planned on doing medical research after college. The job I am currently working at gave me a starting offer that was over 25% more then the best offer that any medical place offered even those that were many more competitive then I could get. I enjoy the job but I can understand why others would not like it. Most that go into biology/chemistry in college plan on becoming a doctor or winning the Nobel Prize. I will never win a Nobel Prize or be a hero, but I do live quite comfortably.
what I want is food preparation down to a science. With ingredient gradings, specific cook times, and guaranteed results.

Cooking a meal and industrial food preparation are two very different things. A chef cooking a meal can be done one way, but it often cannot be scaled up. With big quantities issues of consistency and contamination are frequent problems.

I do nothing with making the food taste 'good,' my whole job is making sure that the 'good' taste occurs in every patch. Also, in any industry setting contamination is a big problem. In food this is a huge focus because everything is going to be eaten. Chemists are important because cooking food is like every other chemical reaction and chemists are trained on how to scale up reactions.
Nice, so on a typical day what do you usually do?

A lot of it is standard testing. Most tests could be done by someone that has finished introductory chemistry. Higher level chemistry classes are needed for solving problems. Every X number of patches needs to get inspected for both quality and contamination. The quality and contamination testing is based on the produce. If a test returns a undesirable result it becomes a question of figuring out what went wrong and how bad the effects are. Occasionally a new product is introduced and the chemist has to make sure that all needed testing standards are met for this new product or the tests have to be created for them.
